original_question: Conjecture: Let G be a finite additive abelian group with |G| odd. Then any subset A of G with |A| = n > 2 can be written as {a1,..., an } in such a way that all the sums a1 + a2, a2 + a3,..., an−1 + an, an + a1 are distinct.
target_in_paper: The draft does not match arXiv:1401.0300, which is The Kourovka Notebook; it matches Conjecture 3.3(i) in Zhi-Wei Sun's "Some new problems in additive combinatorics". ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content of Conjecture 3.3(i): the ambient object is a finite additive abelian group of odd order; the input is a subset A of size n>2; one seeks an ordering of the elements of A; and the required outputs are the n cyclic adjacent sums a1+a2, a2+a3, ..., a_{n-1}+a_n, a_n+a1 being pairwise distinct. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper states the quantifier explicitly as: for every integer n>2, and every n-subset A of a finite additive abelian group G with |G| odd. Writing it this way makes clear that n is quantified first and that A has exactly n distinct elements. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The official formulation asks for a numbering of all n elements of A, i.e. an ordering; your use of set braces {a1,...,an} is slightly imprecise because the condition depends on cyclic order. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))
The paper says the n sums are pairwise distinct; this is the exact formal requirement. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The nearby context in Remark 3.3 explains the intended scope: this conjecture is presented as stronger than Snevily's conjecture in the special case A=B, and the remark also notes a torsion-free analogue. That motivation is not reflected in the draft. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should be kept at Conjecture 3.3(i), not broadened to the neighboring coefficient-2 problem in Conjecture 3.4(i) or to the torsion-free weighted statement of Theorem 1.3. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Is the following conjecture true? For every integer n>2 and every n-element subset A of a finite additive abelian group G of odd order, there exists an ordering A={a1,...,an} such that the n cyclic adjacent sums a1+a2, a2+a3, ..., a_{n-1}+a_n, a_n+a1 are pairwise distinct. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This rewrite is essentially the paper's Conjecture 3.3(i) made fully stand-alone. The draft is already very close, but the paper's exact wording makes the quantified role of n explicit, uses "n-subset"/"numbering" to emphasize that all elements are distinct and ordered, and states the conclusion as pairwise distinct cyclic adjacent sums. Remark 3.3 is the key nearby context: it situates the conjecture relative to Snevily's conjecture and notes the torsion-free analogue. The neighboring Conjecture 3.4(i) and Theorem 1.3 concern a different weighted expression a_i+2a_{i+1}, so they should not replace this target. ([maths.nju.edu.cn](https://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/196a.pdf?utm_source=openai))
